claude.rationale: The slice documents only deregistration/reporting-status facts and explicitly states that no periodic filing or reputable-press source traces a distinct 3-5-year realized trajectory for the acquired HCBF/Harbor Community Bank business: HCBF filed a Form 15-15D within two weeks of the January 1, 2018 close, and EDGAR full-text searches for "Harbor Community Bank" and "HCBF" return no relevant successor disclosures. Because no realized operating outcome for the product/process or process/organization interface is documented, there is no evidence to code either pathway, so both are uncertain rather than 0. The direct acquirer CenterState was itself absorbed into South State via a June 2020 "merger of equals," but the slice provides no realized-outcome evidence about how that or the HCBF combination played out substantively.

grok.rationale: The slice documents that HCBF deregistered within two weeks of closing and that the direct acquirer CenterState itself ceased independent SEC reporting ~2.5 years later after absorption into South State, with no subsequent filings or press tracing any distinct HCBF/Harbor Community Bank operating trajectory. Full-text EDGAR searches for “Harbor Community Bank” and “HCBF” in the 3-5-year window returned no related hits disclosing product/process or process/organization outcomes. Consequently no realized disruption at the product/process interface (p4) or process/organization interface (p5) is documented.

openai.rationale: No periodic SEC filing traces the acquired business as a distinct line item during the 3–5-year outcome window, and EDGAR searches found no relevant Form 10-K disclosures. Accordingly, the slice documents neither product/process disruption nor a fracture between operations and people, management, or culture.
